# worklist — a persisted queue consumed one item per pagination page
# Boots the worklist scenario, runs one drain. The manifest is a two-page
# listing (item-a + item-b, then item-c); the consume step fetches one queue
# head per page and the slice progress write pops it. Across the drain the
# refill fires twice (once per manifest page) and three items are consumed,
# each yielding two events — 5 HTTP exchanges, 6 events in queue order.
# The two steps use different wire encodings: the manifest is plain JSON, while
# each item is a gzip-compressed CSV payload, so the consume step's decode chain
# decompresses then parses CSV rows as events (string-valued fields).
# The spec is loaded live from the embedded template.

exec skopos template show -o spec.yml worklist
replace spec.yml http://localhost:9999 $URL
exec skopos run -i spec.yml --once --trace trace.jsonl --out events.jsonl
normalize trace.jsonl
cmp trace.jsonl want_trace.jsonl
cmp events.jsonl want_events.jsonl

-- want_trace.jsonl --
{"elapsed":"<scrubbed>","iteration":1,"method":"GET","query":{"cursor":"<ref state.cursor>"},"request_headers":{"Accept":"application/json, application/x-ndjson;q=0.9, */*;q=0.1","Authorization":"<redacted>"},"response_body":"body 71 bytes, object-like","started_at":"<scrubbed>","status":200,"step_id":"manifest","url":"$URL_HOST/worklist/manifest"}
{"elapsed":"<scrubbed>","iteration":1,"method":"GET","request_headers":{"Accept":"application/json, application/x-ndjson;q=0.9, */*;q=0.1","Authorization":"<redacted>"},"response_body":"body 94 bytes, non-json","started_at":"<scrubbed>","status":200,"step_id":"consume","url":"$URL_HOST/worklist/items/item-a"}
